title: Stash it
brief:
You are halfway through an edit to `app.txt` on main when you need to check something on the `feature` branch. Try `git switch feature` and read what git says: your half-done edit overlaps with files the switch would overwrite, so git refuses. It is protecting your work.

`git stash` shelves all tracked changes into a real commit object hanging off HEAD, then resets the tree clean. Go look at feature, come back to main, and `git stash pop` brings the work back, unstaged, exactly as you left it.

End state: back on main with the work restored AND committed as "finish the experiment". The pop proves nothing was lost; the commit proves the work is real.

goals.label: The half-done edit survived the round trip

diagnostics.say: That dirty file is why git refuses the switch: app.txt differs between the branches, and switching would overwrite your edit. git stash shelves it first.

hints: Try the switch first and read the refusal. Then: git stash.
git stash, git switch feature, git switch main, git stash pop. Now the edit is back, unstaged.
Finish: git add app.txt, git commit -m "finish the experiment".
